messages:
Maria: Deploybot started staged enable for model zephyr-13b-v2 -> 5% traffic (canaries: us-west-2, eu-west-1). Change window 2026-03-21 18:00-20:00 UTC. tagging @sre-oncall and @DevOps for visibility

deploy-bot: [deploybot] 5777777777 - catalog.enable zephyr-13b-v2 -> 5% canary | regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1 | rollout_id=roll-5777 :white_check_mark:

Jonathan: seeing eu-west-1 p95 jump to ~180ms (baseline ~120ms). Can we hold the EU canary? @sre-oncall any quick reads?

sre-oncall: yep, confirmed a CPU steal / contention blip on two nodes in eu-west-1; tail latency spike correlates with increased batching. digging into node metrics now. will set an alert and hold.

Carol: proposal: pause eu-west-1 and route EU traffic back to zephyr-13b-v1 until we validate the new quantization profile. keep us-west-2 canary running.

Maria: +1. We should do a region-scoped pause/patch so rollout_id remains the same and telemetry stays coherent. Also update fallback ordering for the EU region to prefer v1 while paused.

DevOps: I can patch routing policy. Running the safe operator patch command:
```
./deployctl catalog patch --model zephyr-13b-v2 --region eu-west-1 --action pause --fallback zephyr-13b-v1 --note "latency spike"
```

deploy-bot: ack. Running patch... 5777777789 - patch applied. eu-west-1 standby -> fallback=zephyr-13b-v1. Traffic for eu-west-1 reverted to v1. rollout_id=roll-5777 :white_check_mark:

Jonathan: thanks. Let's observe p50/p95 for the next 15m. If p95 remains >150ms for 10m we keep paused and escalate to a rollback/quantization revert.

sre-oncall: putting a short alert: rule p95_eu > 150ms for 10m -> create incident stub and attach traces. Capturing span traces for affected requests.

Maria: I'll update release notes & internal changelog: note that v2 was enabled in two regions and paused in eu-west-1 due to latency bump; EU customers remain on v1. Will include the config diff and the rollout_id.

Carol: longer-term suggestion — add a fallback weight so we can route a small fraction to a quantized variant in eu for testing without full enable. But for now keep the simple pause/fallback.

Maria: agreed. If metrics recover we can resume eu canary with incremental steps (5% -> 10% -> 20%) using rollout_id roll-5777 and a 10m observation gate between steps.

DevOps: monitoring configured, snapshot link: https://metrics.redwood/internal/dashboards/roll-5777?from=5777777777&to=5777777860

Jonathan: :thumbsup: nice work, folks. I'll follow up in 20m with a quick status update and suggested roll vs rollback decision.
